transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As part of our standard launch-governance process, I need each of you to state any legal condition that must be included in the launch packet before I can give final authorization for the October 1 external release. Let's go around the table — what conditions or requirements does your functional area need included?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a licensing condition before we proceed. My completed license review of the production build identified that module M-17 incorporates an AGPL-licensed library. Under our company's approved proprietary deployment policy, M-17 must be replaced before any external customer access is permitted. This condition must be included in the launch packet, and M-17 must be swapped out before October 1.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a privacy condition before we proceed. The signed design-partner agreement includes specific commitments that are not yet reflected in the standard privacy language in our launch packet. Specifically, customer content may not be used to train or improve our models, and customer content must be deleted within exactly 30 days after account termination. The standard privacy template currently in the launch packet does not include these binding terms. The privacy language must be updated to match these contractual commitments before final authorization for the October 1 external release.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a regulatory condition before we proceed. My intended-use review concluded that the planned language describing automated clinical triage recommendations makes diagnostic claims. The launch materials must instead describe the product as an administrative workflow tool only. This condition must be included in the launch packet — the product description and related materials must be revised to remove any diagnostic-claim language and reframe the product as an administrative workflow tool before final authorization for the October 1 external release.
